title: From Personal Projects to San Francisco
subtitle: Hack Club Undercity
paragraphs: The journey to San Francisco started in May, right after I finished my IB exams.

With a few months before university, I spent my time working on hardware through Hack Club. I started with smaller builds, then designed a custom mechanical keyboard, a HOTAS flight control system, and another keyboard incorporating wireless technology.

Each project gave me something new to explore: PCB design, microcontrollers, firmware, mechanical design, or wireless communication. The possibility of attending a hardware hackathon in San Francisco added some extra motivation.

In July, I attended Hack Club’s Undercity event and worked alongside two teammates from North Carolina. I enjoyed collaborating in person with people I otherwise wouldn’t have met, surrounded by others working on their own hardware ideas.

One highlight was visiting GitHub’s headquarters. After spending so much time using GitHub for my projects, it was interesting to see the company and get a glimpse of San Francisco’s engineering culture.
Looking back, those months were productive in a way I really enjoyed. I learned a lot, built things I was interested in, and visited a city I’d wanted to see for a long time.
I’d recommend Hack Club to other young people interested in programming or hardware. The community gave me opportunities to build and meet people with similar interests.
